payload.name: Preserve explicit facts as atomic memories
payload.description: Use when extracting or updating memories from a message that contains explicitly stated specific facts (relationship origin, dates, locations, occupations) alongside general conversation; preserve each fact separately.
content: When a message explicitly states a specific durable fact (e.g., how a relationship began, a location, a date, an occupation), extract that fact as its own atomic memory candidate with the precise detail, instead of embedding it only in a broad conversation summary.

During memory update/merge, if an existing summary memory lacks a specific fact that was explicitly stated in the source message, ADD a separate memory for that fact (or MERGE it into the relevant subject memory) so the detail remains retrievable.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often collapses several explicit statements into one high-level conversation summary, dropping concrete facts (such as how a relationship began) that later questions need. This Skill instructs extractors to preserve each explicitly stated specific fact as its own atomic memory candidate, while continuing to summarize general chatter. It applies whenever a user reveals a durable personal detail in conversation, especially origin/backstory facts, and does not apply to opinions or non-durable small talk.

payload.name: Preserve explicit current-focus statements during extraction
payload.description: When extracting or updating memories from a message, if the speaker explicitly states what they are focusing on, prioritizing, or working on lately, preserve that claim itself and do not replace it with only the supporting activities.
content: During extraction, identify explicit statements of current focus, priorities, or recent emphasis (phrases like 'I've been focusing on', 'I'm prioritizing', 'lately I've been working on').
Create a memory or enrich the relevant existing memory with the explicit focus claim itself, not only the associated activities or examples.
When the same message also mentions supporting activities, include both the explicit focus claim and the activities so the memory answers questions about focus directly.

candidates.solves: Future questions ask what someone has been focusing on lately. The extraction lost the explicit focus statement and kept only supporting activities, so memory could not answer. Reusable rule: preserve explicit focus/priority claims as primary evidence when extracting, not just examples. Applies when a message states an explicit focus with supporting activities; not when only activities appear.

payload.name: Extract explicit attributed values separately
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly credits a specific person with stressing, teaching, or valuing something, extract that claim as its own memory item.
content: During extraction, when a speaker explicitly attributes a specific value, belief, or instruction to a named person, preserve that claim as a distinct memory, not just as part of a broad summary. Record the person, the specific item, and the speaker's stated intent to apply it.
Link the memory to the source message and choose memory kind 'relationship' for ongoing influence from that person, or 'event' for a one-time statement.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates often condense a conversation into general themes and drop the exact wording of an attributed value or instruction. This skill applies when a speaker explicitly states that a particular person stressed, taught, or valued something specific and that fact can be queried independently later. The rule ensures explicit attributions are preserved as separate, evidence-bound memories rather than being absorbed into a broad summary.

payload.name: Preserve-Explicit-Reasons-In-Event-Memories
payload.description: When a message states an event or decision together with an explicit reason, use this Skill to include that reason in the memory during extraction and to backfill it during updates.
content: During extraction, if a message describes an event or decision and explicitly states why it happened (e.g., 'because', 'so', 'saw X and wanted Y'), include that reason in the candidate memory content.
During update or enrichment, compare the existing memory with earlier source messages; if an explicit reason is missing, add it before appending unrelated details.
Only record reasons that are directly stated; do not infer motives that the speaker did not express.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often records an event or acquisition while dropping the explicit reason given by the speaker, so later 'why' questions cannot be answered from memory. This Skill addresses that by requiring extraction to preserve stated motivations and requiring updates to backfill missing reasons from earlier evidence. It applies to any future event where the speaker explicitly explains why something happened or was done, but not to speculative or unstated causes.

payload.name: Extract each subject's action in multi-event messages
payload.description: When a message reports distinct actions by different people, especially with 'while', 'during', or 'at the same time', extract a separate candidate memory for each subject's event.
content: During extraction, treat each independently verifiable fact in a message as a separate candidate; do not let a prominent topic suppress other subjects.
When a message uses temporal conjunctions such as 'while', 'during', or 'at the same time', extract a distinct memory for each subject's activity on either side of the conjunction.
Do not merge two subjects' distinct events into one memory; if a memory already exists for one part, add the other part as a separate memory or update appropriately.

candidates.solves: Messages often bundle multiple people's concurrent actions using temporal connectors like 'while' or 'during'; extraction can capture only the more salient subject and lose the other, making memories incomplete. This skill provides a targeted rule to split multi-subject temporal clauses into separate extraction candidates, preserving all durable facts in future conversations.

payload.name: Per-Speaker Extraction in Multi-Participant Conversations
payload.description: When extracting memories from a conversation where multiple participants each describe their own feelings, preferences, or experiences, create separate memory candidates per speaker and preserve each speaker's identity and any named locations.
content: During extraction, when multiple speakers express personal feelings or experiences, create a separate memory candidate for each speaker's statement; never merge them into one memory under a single subject.
When a statement uses first-person language ('I', 'me', 'my'), attribute the memory to the speaker of that message, not to another participant mentioned nearby.

Before an ADD, verify the candidate content includes the speaker's identity and any specific locations or context that speaker referenced; if multiple distinct claims exist, extract them as separate memories.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction collapsed a multi-speaker exchange into one memory for a single speaker, losing another participant's expressed feeling so later questions about that participant failed. This applies to any future conversation where multiple people each share personal feelings or experiences: extraction must create per-speaker candidates rather than merging them into one subject's memory.

payload.name: CaptureExplicitSkillAcquisitionMethod
payload.description: Use when extracting or updating memory candidates from a message where a person directly states how they learned a skill (self-taught, taught by someone) to ensure that fact is preserved.
content: During extraction, when a message answers a question about how someone learned or acquired a skill (e.g., self-taught, taught by others), create a distinct candidate fact stating that acquisition method; do not let adjacent supportive details replace it.
Before an UPDATE enrichment, compare the source message's factual claims with the proposed content and include any explicitly stated acquisition method in the enriched memory.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction often captures surrounding details (passion, encouragement) but drops the direct answer about how a person learned a skill. This rule ensures every explicitly stated acquisition method (self-taught vs. taught by someone) is preserved as a durable fact during extraction and update enrichment, so future questions about learning history can be answered from memory.

payload.name: Preserve-Distinct-Actions-In-Memory-Candidates
payload.description: When extracting or updating a memory from a user message that lists multiple specific actions, reasons, or mechanisms (typically joined by 'and' or commas), use this skill to keep each detail instead of merging them into a vague umbrella term.
content: When creating extraction candidates, identify every distinct action, reason, or mechanism the speaker explicitly mentions (e.g., 'help and push'). Keep each one in the candidate content; do not replace a set of concrete verbs with a broader cover term like 'support' that hides which specifics were stated.

When updating an existing memory with new evidence, add the newly mentioned concrete details alongside prior content; do not merge them silently into an existing vague phrase, because a later question may target exactly that detail.

Before finalizing an extraction or update, check that each concrete element from the source message is still recoverable from the memory text; if a paraphrase would cause a later reader to infer a different or narrower meaning, prefer the explicit original phrasing.

candidates.solves: When a user explicitly names multiple distinct actions, reasons, or mechanisms for a single outcome or activity, extraction often compresses them into one vague synonym, dropping details that later questions need. This rule requires preserving each concrete element in memory candidates and updates, so claims about specific causes remain answerable. It applies to any conversation where a message enumerates co-occurring specifics.

payload.name: IncludeGeneralActivityTermsInEventExtraction
payload.description: When extracting event memories from a conversation where a speaker mentions a general activity term (e.g., 'excursions', 'tours', 'sightseeing') plus specific examples, include the general term in the candidate memory.
content: During extraction of event memories, review all speaker messages about the same event. If the speaker uses a broad activity word (e.g., 'went on excursions', 'did sightseeing', 'took tours') alongside specific examples (e.g., 'visited cafes', 'attended yoga classes'), record both the general term and the specific examples in the candidate memory.
Do not treat the specific examples as exhaustive; the general term is an explicit fact that must be preserved.
If the general term appears in a later message about the same event, update or supplement the candidate to include it rather than only keeping the earlier specific details.

candidates.solves: During extraction of event memories, the agent summarized a trip by listing specific activities (yoga, cafes, temple) but omitted the speaker's explicit general statement 'we went on many excursions', making the memory incomplete. This happens when a speaker uses both a general activity term and specific examples. The skill ensures the general category is preserved alongside details, applying to any future conversation with similar summary-and-example descriptions.

payload.name: Preserve all distinct attributes in multi-topic preference extraction
payload.description: When a user message expresses separate preferences or evaluations for two or more distinct activities/topics, extract each fully or combine without omitting any subject or attribute.
content: During extraction, if one message contains multiple distinct subjects/activities, each with its own evaluation or preference, create separate memory candidates for each distinct subject-attribute pair (or one candidate that explicitly lists all subjects and their attributes).
Do not let the last-mentioned or most emotionally salient subject cause earlier subjects/attributes to be dropped; check the full message for every explicit qualitative claim.
Before finalizing a candidate, verify that all memory-worthy claims in the message are represented either in that candidate or in sibling candidates from the same message.

candidates.solves: When one user message gives separate evaluations for multiple distinct activities/topics, extraction must preserve each subject-attribute pair instead of dropping earlier ones. Applies to any future message with multiple independently described subjects in one turn; the failure is selective extraction that omits one stated attribute.

payload.name: Preserve actor and specific topic in interpersonal event memories
payload.description: When constructing event memories from messages where one person reports an action done to them by others, include who did it and the exact subject (e.g., 'friends mocked his weight') in the memory content.
content: During extraction and update, for any event where the subject is the target of another's action (mock, praise, criticize, help, etc.), capture the actor and the specific topic or attribute in the memory content, not just the subject's resulting feelings or decisions.
Avoid paraphrasing that drops explicit participants or the exact object of the action; if the original names the actor and the topic, both must appear in the memory.
Before finalizing a memory, verify it answers 'who did this?' and 'about what?' from its content alone; add any missing details from the source message if not.

candidates.solves: Event extraction from first-person accounts of interpersonal actions often keeps only the subject's reaction and drops the actor and the exact topic, making memories unable to answer who or what questions. This rule applies when another person performed an action toward the subject; it does not apply to internal states or solo actions. Preserve the full predicate in the memory content.

payload.name: Per-speaker subject attribution in scheduling memories
payload.description: When a scheduling conversation contains a cancellation and a new proposed time from different speakers, use during extraction to assign each fact to its own speaker.
content: During extraction, treat each message as the source for its own facts: resolve 'I'/'my' to the message speaker before assigning the memory subject.
When a candidate bundles a rescheduling reason and a new proposed time, verify each clause's subject independently; do not extend the first subject to later clauses uttered by a different speaker.
If a candidate combines statements from multiple speakers, output separate memory candidates or set the subject per clause so each person's availability and conflict are stored correctly.

candidates.solves: The failure occurred when an extraction candidate bundled a rescheduling conflict and a later proposed time into one memory under a single subject, even though the facts came from different speakers in a multi-turn scheduling conversation. This rule enforces speaker-aware subject resolution for first-person statements and prevents cross-turn subject leakage when extracting scheduling memories.

payload.name: preserve-activity-qualifiers-during-extraction
payload.description: When extracting an activity or event from user speech, preserve explicit intensity/degree and descriptive qualifiers such as 'nonstop' or 'futuristic setting' in the memory content instead of summarizing them away.
content: During extraction, for each stated activity, capture all explicit modifiers that convey intensity, frequency, duration, or notable attributes; do not drop them in favor of a generic summary.

If a single message contains two distinct activities, create separate memory entries (or at least keep each activity's modifiers attached to its own clause) so that later queries about one activity can be answered from evidence.
When writing the memory content, use the speaker's own qualitative terms (e.g., 'nonstop', 'futuristic setting') rather than replacing them with an interpretation like 'enjoyed'.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is an extraction candidate that collapsed two activities and omitted explicit qualifiers ('nonstop', 'futuristic setting') that a later question asked about. The general failure mechanism is lossy summarization during extraction, where intensity/descriptive details are dropped because they seem secondary. This applies to any future session where a user states an activity with modifiers; the memory must retain those modifiers to support later grounding. The rule is bounded to extraction of activity/event memories; it does not apply to opinions or general likes.

payload.name: Preserve shared-picture description in extraction
payload.description: When a speaker shares or references a picture and explains what it shows or its origin, use during extraction and memory updates to capture the sharing action and the picture's described content rather than only an inferred ownership.
content: During extraction, if a message contains or refers to a shared picture and the speaker states what it depicts or where it comes from (e.g., creator, source, subject), create a memory that records the sharing action and the picture's described content/origin. Do not replace this with only an ownership or possession fact about a related object. When updating existing memories, if the shared picture's description is missing but the message supports it, add it to the relevant memory rather than leaving only the object-related detail.

candidates.solves: The diagnosed cause is that extraction reduced a shared-photo explanation to an inferred ownership fact, so later questions about the shared picture cannot be answered. This skill applies whenever a speaker shares or references a picture and provides details about its content or origin; it ensures the sharing act and the picture's described attributes are durably captured during extraction and preserved on updates, making the memory answerable for future picture-related queries.

payload.name: Extract every item from enumerated fact lists
payload.description: When a user message contains a list of multiple distinct facts, preferences, or activities about the same subject, use this during extraction to preserve all listed items.
content: During candidate extraction, if a message enumerates multiple distinct facts, preferences, or activities (e.g., joined by 'and', commas, or 'also'), capture every listed item in the memory content or split them into separate candidates.
Do not let elaboration on one item cause other listed items to be dropped; include the complete enumeration even when one item receives more explanation.

candidates.solves: When a user message lists multiple distinct facts or preferences about the same subject (e.g., several hobbies joined by 'and', commas, or 'also'), the extraction stage may preserve only the most elaborated item, causing other listed facts to be missing from memory. The reusable mechanism is complete enumeration capture: every discrete item in the list must be represented in extracted memory content or as separate candidates. This applies to any future message containing an enumeration of durable facts, and does not require knowing the gold answer.

payload.name: ExtractExplicitMediaFacts
payload.description: When a user shares a photo or media and explicitly states a factual detail about it (e.g., location, time, what it shows), use this during extraction to preserve that specific fact in memory instead of only the general discussion.
content: During extraction, when a speaker shares a photo or other media and explicitly states a factual detail about it (e.g., location, time, content, owner), create a memory that records that specific fact, not just the general conversation topic.

When later messages elaborate on the shared media, extract the concrete factual statements from the original sharing message into an event or relationship memory, and avoid merging them into a vague thematic summary.

candidates.solves: When constructing memories from a conversation, an agent may summarize the general discussion and omit concrete facts explicitly stated about a shared photo or media. This Skill applies to future sessions where a user shares a picture and states a specific attribute (location, time, subject, etc.); extraction should preserve that fact as its own memory, not only the topical conversation.

payload.name: PreserveMultiStageTimelineFacts
payload.description: When extracting a person's history of an activity across multiple stages (school levels, teams, jobs) or when later messages add durations, use and update explicit stage-specific facts instead of collapsing into a generic summary.
content: During extraction, if a message lists an activity across multiple named stages or institutions (e.g., middle school, high school, college), extract each stage as an explicit fact or ordered list including any stated years/durations; do not collapse them into 'since childhood' or another generic summary.
During CRUD, if a later message adds a missing stage detail or duration for an existing multi-stage memory, update that memory instead of keeping only the earlier general summary.

candidates.solves: A construction agent often collapses a multi-stage timeline into one generic memory, dropping concrete stages and durations. This skill preserves each explicitly mentioned stage as its own fact and updates existing memories when later messages supply durations, so future questions about specific stages can be answered. Applies to any multi-stage history (education, career, team membership); not to single-fact statements.

payload.name: Preserve-all-enumerated-facts-in-memory
payload.description: When a message contains an explicit list of distinct items, attributes, or reasons (e.g., separated by commas or 'and'), use during extraction to keep every listed element in the memory content.
content: During extraction, if a statement lists multiple distinct elements (e.g., several things someone found relaxing, preferences, or experiences), preserve each listed element explicitly in the memory content; do not replace the list with a summary that omits any item.
When writing the memory, keep the enumerated facts as separate recognizable phrases so a later evidence check can match each element independently.

candidates.solves: Prevents extraction from dropping items when a user explicitly enumerates multiple distinct facts (e.g., things found relaxing, reasons, preferences, experiences). This applies whenever a source message contains a comma-separated or 'and'-joined list of separate elements; it does not apply to a single experience that can be safely paraphrased in condensed wording.

payload.name: Preserve-explicit-item-lists-in-extraction
payload.description: When a message explicitly lists concrete recommended items or steps, retain the full enumeration in extraction and memory updates instead of summarizing it away.
content: During extraction, when a message contains an explicit enumeration of concrete items (e.g., supplies, steps, ingredients, resources), preserve each listed item in the candidate content; do not replace the enumeration with a generic phrase like 'recommend supplies' or 'various items'.
When updating an existing memory with such a list, include the specific items in the updated content so later queries can retrieve them.

candidates.solves: When a speaker explicitly lists concrete items (supplies, steps, ingredients, resources) in a recommendation or plan, extraction candidates often collapse the list into a vague summary and lose answerable facts. This skill ensures future extractions and memory updates preserve the full stated enumeration, applying whenever explicit lists appear, without requiring invention of unstated details.

payload.name: Capture-explicit-missing-object-in-nostalgia-statements
payload.description: When extracting from a statement where a speaker says they miss or long for a past experience, include the exact activity and the specific quality or object they explicitly miss.
content: During candidate extraction, if a speaker says they miss or long for a past experience, capture both the general activity and the precise thing they say they miss, such as the specific emotional quality or aspect named. Do not let a broader paraphrase of the activity replace the explicitly named object or quality.

Store the specific missed object as part of the memory content; if the speaker later elaborates on the same memory, preserve or enrich that detail rather than overwriting it with the general activity.

candidates.solves: When a speaker says they miss or long for a past experience, extraction candidates often retain only the broad activity and drop the explicitly named object or emotional quality they say they miss. This skill requires the precise missed thing to appear in the candidate, so later queries about that specific aspect can be answered. It applies to nostalgic or missing statements on any topic, but not to routine descriptions that name no explicit missed object.

operations.name: Preserve Explicit Facts as Atomic Memories
operations.description: Use when extracting or updating memories from a message that contains explicitly stated specific facts, lists, or attributes; preserve each as its own memory or distinct element.
content: When a message explicitly states a specific durable fact (e.g., how a relationship began, a location, a date, an occupation, a reason, a focus, an attributed value, a skill acquisition method, a shared picture's content), extract that fact as its own atomic memory candidate with the precise detail, instead of embedding it only in a broad conversation summary.

When a message enumerates multiple distinct items, attributes, or reasons (joined by 'and', commas, or 'also'), preserve every listed element in the memory content or split them into separate candidates; do not let elaboration on one item cause others to be dropped.

During memory update/merge, if an existing summary memory lacks a specific fact that was explicitly stated in the source message, ADD a separate memory for that fact (or MERGE it into the relevant subject memory) so the detail remains retrievable.
Preserve explicit qualifiers, intensity/degree modifiers, and the speaker's own wording (e.g., 'nonstop', 'futuristic setting') rather than replacing them with a generic interpretation.

When multiple speakers express personal facts, create separate memory candidates per speaker and attribute first-person statements to the correct speaker; do not merge distinct subjects' events or attributes into one memory.
operations.reason: All candidates share the same underlying failure mechanism: lossy extraction that drops explicitly stated facts, lists, or attributes. Merging into one Skill that enforces atomic preservation of explicit details.
